post.description:
Remove a sign-up that has no account, and every code tied to its address: for a removal request by email. Someone
with an account is refused (409): deleting the account removes the sign-up with it. The reason is kept in the audit
log with the sign-up's number, never the address.

End a person's beta access now, and email them that their access has ended. For someone who has not made an
account yet, withdraw their code instead (nothing to email). The reason is kept in the audit log and never sent.

Stop an invite being used. People who already signed up with it keep their accounts.

post.description:
Load the research CSV (the 48 columns, one row per rule set): new rule sets are added, changed ones updated and
the rest left alone. Rows that cannot be read are listed by line; the others are still loaded.

put.description:
Replace one template's values and flags. Only the kinds of the values are checked (the research leaves cells
empty on purpose); people's verified rule sets are copies and do not change.

get.description: One account in full (still counters and facts only). Looking is itself written to the audit log.

put.description: Put the person on this plan whatever else they have, even a lower one. Replaces an override already in force.

post.description: End the override in force. (A POST rather than a DELETE, so the reason travels in a body.)
Sign the person out everywhere, without suspending them.
Mark the account for deletion a week away, as if the person had asked. They can cancel it by signing in.
Sign the person out everywhere and refuse their sign-ins until restored. Their data is untouched.

get.description: Every account with its progress against the firm's rules (closed trades only; see `api/progress.py`).

post.description: Schedule this account's deletion for a week from now, and sign out everywhere.

get.description: Every account, by name. Archived ones (passed, failed or closed) are included unless `include_archived=false`.

post.description:
A new account with no rules and no fees yet (set those next). The purchase date is required: it decides which
version of the firm's rules applies.

get.description:
Every active account against its verified rules (status, breach-to-payout bar, payout readiness, consistency,
inactivity, each rule's result) and the totals. Closed trades only: see `compliance.py` for what that means.

put.description:
Change an account's name, firm, type, size, starting balance, purchase date and phase. Changing the type
reclassifies its trades.

post.description:
Mark an account as finished (an evaluation passes, fails or is closed; a funded account fails or is closed).
Its trades stay; views leave them out unless asked.

get.description: Dollars per contract, round trip, by contract root ("NQ"); `*` is the rate for any other contract.

delete.description: Remove a contract's own rate (it falls back to `*`). Stored trades are recalculated in the same change.

put.description: Set the rate for a contract root. The account's stored trades are recalculated in the same change.

get.description: The account's costs and payouts, oldest first.

post.description: Record money spent on the account (a fee) or received from it (a payout). The amount is always positive.

delete.description: Delete one entry and answer with what is left of the account's ledger.

post.description:
Stop offering "Evaluation passed: set up your funded account" on the Accounts tab. The account's settings still
offer it.

get.description:
The account's payouts, oldest first, with their numbers and the lifetime totals, and the split its rules promise
(the default for the next one).

post.description:
Log a payout: the gross the firm paid out and the trader's split (net = gross x split, to the cent). Without a
split, the one in the account's rules is used; a fee is counted as a cost of the business.

get.description: The rules the person verified for this account; null when there are none yet.

put.description:
Verify the account's rules: every value is copied in, so a later change to the template never changes them. The
previous rule set is kept as history. Each field that is wrong is named in the 422's `errors` (`values.<field>`).
Set the firm's rules (profit target, drawdown, trailing, daily loss limit). A rule left null is not tracked.

get.description: What has happened to this account lately.
Across every account, archived ones included: what the accounts cost, what they paid out, how evaluations ended.
The headline numbers, equity curves, daily results, score and per-account results for the filtered trades.
Which trading days from `start` to `end` (at most 400 days) have a note. No content: only the days.
The note for one trading day; an empty one when nothing is written.

put.description: Replace the note for a trading day. Answers with what was stored (a note with no visible text removes it).

get.description:
Everything stored for this account, as one ZIP: CSV tables, notes as HTML and text, the screenshot files, and a
manifest with checksums.

200.description: A ZIP of everything stored for the account (see manifest.json inside)

429.description: Too many exports are being built right now; try again shortly

post.description: Use a plan code. Answers the plan the person is on afterwards.

get.description: Every import, newest first (undone ones included, marked).

post.description: Import the file into the account. Rows already stored are left alone, so importing a file twice is safe.

What importing this file into this account would do: counts, problems, and the first rows with a status each.
Nothing is saved (the import runs inside a transaction that is rolled back), so the preview is exactly what the
real import would do.
Remove what the import brought in (rows another import also holds stay) and regroup what is left.
What undoing the import would remove, without removing it.

get.description:
The filtered trades broken down by contract, weekday, time of day, hold time, tag or account, with the dashboard's
statistics for each group. The date range and the other filters are the dashboard's.
Every rule field (name, kind, group, label, choices, hint) in the form's order, and the groups in order.

The firms' rule sets that can apply to an account bought on `purchased_on`: the versions in force by then, and
those the research could not date. The latest version of each firm + program + size + phase is preselected. Without
a date every version is listed and none is preselected.

One firm's rule set in full, with what the research could not confirm (`flags`) and the source's own words for
cells that were not a clean value (`source_notes`).

delete.description: Log out everywhere else: every other working session of this account ends; this one stays.

get.description: Where this account is signed in now.

delete.description: Sign out one other place. Someone else's id, an ended one and an unknown one all answer the same 404.
Delete a category, its tags, and those tags' links to trades (the trades themselves stay).

get.description: Every category and tag (each with the number of trades that carry it) and the colours on offer.

post.description: A new tag in a category, or the one already there under that name (any capitalization).

delete.description: Delete a tag everywhere, including from the trades that carry it.

put.description:
Rename, recolour or move a tag. The trades carrying it keep it; a name already used in the target category is
a conflict (merge the two instead).

post.description: Move every trade from this tag to another, then delete this one. A trade that carried both keeps one.

get.description: One page of the trade log, with the total count and net result of everything the filters match.

Everything about one trade. Another user's trade and a missing one are both a 404: they look the same. Its
screenshots carry the address of their image, or none on a server that has nowhere to keep files.

The trades either side of this one in the list the person came from (same filters, search and order). A trade
that is not theirs and one that does not exist are both a 404, as for the trade itself: they look the same.

put.description: Replace a trade's notes. Answers with what was stored (a note with no visible text is stored as empty).

post.description: Add an image (PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP, up to 10 MB and 50 million pixels) to a trade.

delete.description: Delete one screenshot of a trade. Answers with the ones that are left.
Take a tag off a trade (not on it is fine); the tag stays for other trades. Answers with the trade's tags.

put.description: Put a tag on a trade (already there is fine). Answers with the trade's tags.

post.description: End this session. The page then sends the browser to `redirect`, which ends the provider's own session too.

get.description: The bytes of one of the signed-in person's screenshots.
